The image shows soybean seeds held in a hand. Key observations:
- Seeds are the affected plant part (seed/grain)
- Most seeds show purple/violet discoloration patches on a yellow/tan background
- Some seeds appear completely yellow/healthy, others have large purple blotches
- The purple staining is irregular, covering portions of the seed coat
- No white mold, no lesions on leaves — this is purely seed symptom

This is a classic presentation of **Purple Seed Stain**, caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*. The characteristic purple/violet discoloration on the seed coat, varying from small spots to large blotches, is the defining symptom. This is distinct from Cercospora leaf blight (which affects leaves), as this image shows only seeds with purple staining.
